title: Talking Verbs
objectives: I can tell how someone speaks with eight exact talking verbs.
I can use a talking verb instead of the word said.
I can choose the best talking verb for a story part.
I can say or write a sentence with a talking verb.
rationale: Second graders retell dialogue with said again and again. These eight verbs give them exact choices: how loudly someone speaks (whisper, mumble, announce), what they say it for (complain, suggest, promise), and how talk goes back and forth (reply, interrupt). Children can act every verb out, so meaning is clear before they read. The verbs also show -ed endings in retelling, which sets up later units, and answer, explain, and question from grade 1 are revisited as the replies and suggestions that follow them.

words.def: To speak very softly so few can hear.
words.ex: The children whispered while the baby slept.
words.ex2: Mia whispered a secret into her friend's ear.
words.nonExample: Shouting across the playground is not whispering.

apps.academic: In the library, we whisper so others can read.
apps.spoken: Can you whisper that? The baby is asleep.
apps.writing: Use whispered to show that a character is being quiet or secret.

cloze.s: The class had to ___ in the library so no one was bothered.

cloze2.s: "Be quiet," Ben ___ so the sleeping puppy would not wake.

misuse.s: The girl whispered loudly so the whole bus could hear her.
misuse.why: To whisper is to speak softly, not loudly.

visual.alt: A child holding a finger to her lips and leaning toward a friend's ear.

words.def: To speak in a low, unclear way.
words.ex: Tom mumbled his answer, so nobody could hear it.
words.ex2: The sleepy boy mumbled something about breakfast.
words.nonExample: Speaking clearly and loudly is not mumbling.

apps.academic: Speak up if people cannot hear you when you mumble.
apps.spoken: I could not hear you because you mumbled.
apps.writing: Use mumbled for a character who is shy, tired, or unsure.

cloze.s: I could not understand Leo because he ___ the words into his scarf.

cloze2.s: When the teacher called on her, Kayla looked down and began to ___.

misuse.s: She mumbled each word clearly and every person understood her.
misuse.why: Mumbling is unclear speech, so clear words are the opposite.

visual.alt: A boy with his chin tucked in and a small, faint speech bubble.

words.def: To tell everyone something important out loud.
words.ex: The principal announced that school would close early.
words.ex2: Our teacher announced the winner of the spelling contest.
words.nonExample: Keeping a secret to yourself is not announcing it.

apps.academic: The speaker will announce the next group to read.
apps.spoken: I have big news to announce!
apps.writing: Use announced when a character shares news with a crowd.

cloze.s: The loudspeaker will ___ the bus numbers so everyone knows where to go.

cloze2.s: Dad stood up and ___ the big news: we were getting a puppy!

misuse.s: The mayor announced the news in a whisper that nobody could hear.
misuse.why: To announce is to tell everyone clearly, so it cannot be a whisper no one hears.

visual.alt: A person speaking into a microphone beside a loudspeaker.

words.def: To say you are not happy about something.
words.ex: Sam complained that the soup was too hot.
words.ex2: The campers complained about the rain all afternoon.
words.nonExample: Saying thank you for a gift is not complaining.

apps.academic: Instead of only complaining, tell what would help.
apps.spoken: I do not want to complain, but it is too cold.
apps.writing: Use complained to show a character who is unhappy about something.

cloze.s: Dev likes to ___ when his shoes get wet and cold.

cloze2.s: The neighbors ___ about the loud music coming from the party.

misuse.s: Ella complained that her ice cream was the best treat ever and thanked the cook.
misuse.why: Complaining means saying you are unhappy, but Ella is happy.

visual.alt: A frowning child with a cross face and a speech bubble.

words.def: To offer an idea for someone to think about.
words.ex: Grace suggested a walk to the park after lunch.
words.ex2: The librarian suggested a funny book about frogs.
words.nonExample: Telling someone they must do it is not a suggestion.

apps.academic: I suggest that we read the directions first.
apps.spoken: Can I suggest a different game?
apps.writing: Use suggested to show a character offering an idea, not giving an order.

cloze.s: Can I ___ that we sit by the window so we can watch the snow?

cloze2.s: Jo ___ a game of tag when the class got bored.

misuse.s: Mark suggested that everyone must obey him and nobody else could share an idea.
misuse.why: A suggestion is an idea others can accept or not, not an order.

visual.alt: A girl with a light bulb over her head talking to a friend.

words.def: To say you will surely do something.
words.ex: Lena promised to feed the fish every morning.
words.ex2: Dad promised that we would stop for ice cream.
words.nonExample: Saying you might do something is not a promise.

apps.academic: I promise to share the crayons.
apps.spoken: I promise I will be quiet.
apps.writing: Use promised to show that a character will keep their word.

cloze.s: I ___ to bring your book back tomorrow, and I always keep my word.

cloze2.s: Mom ___ to take us swimming if we cleaned our room.

misuse.s: Ben promised to help and then said he would never do it.
misuse.why: A promise means you will surely do it, so saying never is the opposite.

visual.alt: Two children shaking hands next to a gold star.

words.def: To break in while someone is speaking.
words.ex: Please do not interrupt me while I read this page.
words.ex2: A loud siren interrupted our quiet reading time.
words.nonExample: Waiting your turn to talk is not interrupting.

apps.academic: Raise your hand so you do not interrupt.
apps.spoken: Sorry to interrupt, but I have a question.
apps.writing: Use interrupted to show a character cutting in on someone.

cloze.s: It is rude to ___ when your friend is still telling her story.

cloze2.s: The bell ___ our lesson, so we lined up for lunch.

misuse.s: Nina waited quietly until her friend finished, so she interrupted her.
misuse.why: Waiting until someone finishes is not interrupting.

visual.alt: A child raising a hand while another child is talking.

words.def: To answer someone by speaking or writing.
words.ex: Zoe replied to the letter from her grandmother.
words.ex2: When I asked a question, my teacher replied with a smile.
words.nonExample: Staying silent when someone asks you something is not replying.

apps.academic: Reply to the question with a full sentence.
apps.spoken: I will reply to your text after school.
apps.writing: Use replied after a question to show what the next speaker says.

cloze.s: Mom sent me a text, and I will ___ to it after I finish my homework.

cloze2.s: When the teacher asked a question, Omar ___ with the right answer.

misuse.s: Pam replied to the question by saying nothing at all.
misuse.why: To reply is to answer, and saying nothing is not an answer.

visual.alt: A child writing back to answer a letter.

words.frame: When someone asks me a question, I reply by ___.

passage.title: Pancake Morning
paras: Maya whispered so the baby would sleep. Her brother mumbled from his bed. Dad announced, "Pancakes are ready!"
Her brother began to complain that the syrup was cold, so Maya suggested hot water. "Good idea," he replied. "I promise to say thank you."

qs.q: What does "mumbled" mean in the story?
choices: spoke in a low, unclear way
qs.why: Maya's brother is sleepy, so his words are low and hard to hear.

choices: She did not want to wake the baby.
qs.why: The story says she whispered so she would not wake the baby.

qs.q: What did Maya suggest for the cold syrup?
qs.why: The story says Maya suggested hot water.

write.prompt: Write or tell about a time you whispered or made a promise. Use a talking verb.
write.frame: I whispered when ___. I promised to ___.

study.task: Sort the eight verbs into quiet voices and loud voices. Pick one verb and act it out for a partner without saying it. Your partner guesses the verb.

sentences: Write a sentence about something you would whisper and tell why.
Write a sentence about one thing you can promise to do at home.
Write a sentence about a time it is not polite to interrupt.

given: She did not want to wake the baby.
combine.model: Mika whispered because she did not want to wake the baby.

given: He said the class could plant a garden.
combine.model: Ray suggested that the class plant a garden.

discuss: When do you need to whisper at school? When do you need to announce something?
What is the difference between a complaint and a suggestion?
produce.explain: Explain how complain and suggest are different. Use both words.

argue.prompt: Is it ever okay to interrupt? Say yes or no and give one reason.
argue.frame: I think it is ___ to interrupt because ___.

constructed.prompt: Tell about a time to whisper and a time to announce. Use both words.
look: names a place or reason for each
shows that one is soft and one is loud
constructed.model: I whisper in the library so others can read. I announce news at a class meeting so everyone hears.

constructed.prompt: A friend asks you to bring a book tomorrow. Write what you reply and what you promise.
look: makes sense as an answer to the friend
constructed.model: I replied, "Yes, I can." I promise to bring the book in my backpack.

teacher.overview: Children learn eight verbs that say exactly how people talk and use them in place of said when they retell stories and describe real conversations. Most verbs can be acted out, so start with movement and voice, then connect to the words. The unit revisits answer, explain, and question as the replies and ideas that follow talk.

notes.va.whisper.v: Have children whisper and then shout the same sentence. Tie whisper to places that need it, such as a library. Whisper is not the same as secret, but the two often go together.
notes.va.mumble.v: Children often think mumbling is just being quiet. Contrast it with whisper: a whisper can be clear, a mumble is hard to understand. Model both with the same sentence.
notes.va.announce.v: Stress that announce is for telling many people something important. Practice with a pretend loudspeaker. Spanish speakers have the cognate anunciar.
notes.va.complain.v: Model that complaining means telling what is wrong. Move to suggest by asking, What could we do about it? Keep the tone gentle so children do not feel scolded.
notes.va.suggest.v: A suggestion is an idea, not an order. Practice with the frame I suggest that we, then ask partners to accept or offer a different idea.
notes.va.promise.v: A promise is something you say you will surely do. Teach only the verb sense here; the noun sense (a promise) can follow naturally. Ask what happens when a promise is broken.
notes.va.interrupt.v: Use a role play with a partner talking and a child raising a hand to wait. Interrupt is not always bad, for example a fire alarm, so add that nuance in discussion.
notes.va.reply.v: Reply means to answer back. Link it to the grade 1 word answer and to writing a note back to a friend. Reply can be spoken or written.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The book says, "I can't hear you," because Leo mumbled. If he mumbled, his words were low and unclear. I could say mumbled instead of said. Now I know how he spoke.'
discuss: Which talking verb tells that someone is unhappy? Which tells that someone has an idea?
When would a person need to announce something at school?
misconceptions: Children may use whisper and mumble as the same word. A whisper can be clear; a mumble is not.
Some children think complain is always rude. Help them see that saying what is wrong, calmly, can lead to a suggestion.
Interrupt is not only about voice; it can be a sound or an event, like a bell.
extend: Collect other words children know instead of said and add them to a class chart.
Retell a familiar story with a different talking verb for each character.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit answer, explain, and question by asking children to reply to a question, then explain how they answered. Use whisper and announce in the next unit's routines.

frames: He mumbled, so I could not ___.
wida.oral: Say the same sentence three ways: as a whisper, a mumble, and an announcement. Your partner names the verb you used.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (susurrar, mascullar, anunciar, quejarse, sugerir, prometer, interrumpir, responder) not reviewed by a native speaker; mascullar for mumble is a regional choice.
interrupt is the one target word not used in the passage (kept short for readability); it appears in examples and practice instead.
promise is taught as a verb only; the noun sense (a promise) is not taught here.
